Q: How to add Hilt dependencies on "libs.versions.toml" file in android studio A:

By default, this plugin is configured to use KAPT instead of KSP, so we fix this issues by following these steps:

When using KSP with Hilt, enabling enableAggregatingTask ensures proper code generation and helps avoid potential issues during compilation, so add this line in your app-level Gradle file:

hilt{
    enableAggregatingTask = true
}

Also, the ksp version must match your kotlin version. I suggest defining it explicitly in case Gradle cannot resolve it. So, in your libs.versions.toml add the following line:

kspVersion="1.9.20-1.0.14"

Happy Coding :)

Q: How to generate Insert statement from PGAdmin4 Tool? A:

Follow these screenshots to export as INSERT statements:

Right click on target table and select Backup.

Use the Plain format on the General tab and select the output file:

Then activate the Query Options tab and activate the "Query Options" switch:

Click on the "Backup" button.

You should see SQL like this one in the export file:

Q: How do I handle read system calls for HPC? A:

What about using the standard library functions? They are transparently buffered which can dramatically reduce the count of system calls. If that is not enough you can even use setvbuf with a larger buffer (default size is the system dependent constant BUFSIZ).

Q: Represent a specific date and time as seen in specific time zone, using Java A:

Avoid legacy date-time classes.

Never use the terribly flawed legacy date-time classes such as Date, Calendar, SimpleDateFormat, etc.

Use only the modern java.time classes built into Java 8+. This industry-leading date-time framework was led by the man who also led its predecessor, the Joda-Time framework.

java.time

You want the specify a date and a time-of-day as seen in a particular time zone.

Represent the date portion.

LocalDate date = LocalDate.of( 2013 , Month.SEPTEMBER , 1 ) ;

Represent the time portion.

LocalTime time = LocalTime.of( 12 , 15 ) ;  // Quarter past noon. 24-hour clock.

Represent your time zone.

Unfortunately you used a pseudo-zone of IST. Such 2-4 letter codes are not standardized, and are not even unique! Do you mean Ireland Standard Time? India Standard Time? Real time zone names have a format of Continent/Region such as Europe/Dublin or Asia/Kolkata.

ZoneId zone = ZoneId.of( "Asia/Kolkata" ) ;

Apply that zone to our date and time to determine a moment, a ZonedDateTime object.

ZonedDateTime zdt = ZonedDateTime.of( date , time , zone ) ;

See this code run at Ideone.com. Result matches your expectation.

2013-09-01T12:15+05:30[Asia/Kolkata]

You can generate automatically localized text by way of DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDateTime if you so desire.
